rom.title_romanized: Dragon Ball Z - Chou Gokuuden - Kakusei Hen
rom.title_note: The original Japanese title is not reproduced here: repository policy keeps original-language text out of tracked files. It can be read directly from the ROM header.
rom.notes: 2 MiB LoROM (slow), ROM+RAM+battery, no expansion chip. Regions below are only those verified so far; every unlisted byte is reported as unknown on purpose.

regions.name: Reset vector stub: SEI CLD CLC XCE SEP #$30, STZ.w $4200, LDA.b #$80, STA.w $2100, JML $808012
Bank 0 extended-header lead-in, ASCII "B2A2ZJ" then padding; purpose not yet established
Bank 0 native-mode vectors are entirely $FF; the game installs its own vector table at runtime rather than using the stock LoROM vectors

Reviewed start of a 5,041-byte all-$FF run allocated through $80:EDB2 to the translated dual-format compositor, 120-entry glyph-code table, and bounded one-row name redraw with explicit name-surface dimensions; exact and 24-bit ROM scans found no original reference to the entry point

Reviewed portion of Bank 01's trailing all-$FF run allocated to the mode-aware name/password insertion dispatcher, picker loader, translated name insertion, and cursor routines. WRAM $0216 selects translated packed-Latin insertion only for fresh name entry; password mode reproduces the displaced comparison and rejoins the original insertion/redraw path at $81:8ADD. Decoded Bank 01 control flow has no original target in this interval
Reviewed all-$FF padding allocated to two relocated Latin name-picker streams and two 85-word Latin selection maps; original password pages and maps remain at $84:A3E0/$84:A4D0 and $81:8D56/$81:8E00
Command-$08 lower glyph-source region used by stream codes $0100-$02D0; each displayed glyph reads four 16-byte blocks at +$000, +$010, +$100, and +$110
Command-$08 upper glyph-source region used by stream codes $0900-$0A30; each displayed glyph reads four 16-byte blocks at +$000, +$010, +$100, and +$110
Command-$08 middle glyph-source bank used by stream codes $0500-$08F7; displayed glyphs are assembled from four 16-byte 2bpp blocks
Scenario root selection and byte-command interpreter loop; $49 is the end condition
Scenario command dispatch table: 73 little-endian handler words for values $00-$48; entry $00 is unresolved $0000
Scenario selector table: 370 three-byte slots; 356 non-null pointers (355 unique targets), 14 null slots, targeting CPU banks $91-$93

text_encoding.evidence: A scan for Shift-JIS double-byte runs across the whole image yielded 159 candidate runs totalling 2236 characters, but every significant run is a repeating byte pair such as e849e849e849 rather than readable text. No genuine Shift-JIS text was found.
text_encoding.note: The character encoding is custom: possibly a flat glyph index, possibly a dictionary or compressed scheme. Rule 17 requires establishing this from evidence before any translation is attempted.

hardware_register_access.evidence: Bank $00 contains direct absolute stores configuring DMA channels and the VRAM data port. For example, the routine around CPU $00:838A writes DMA B-bus destination $18, meaning PPU register $2118, while the corresponding DMA source bank is $7E (WRAM). Other direct stores set $43x2-$43x4 source fields and $420B DMA enable bits.
hardware_register_access.note: The literal $18 in the DMA setup is a B-bus register number, not ROM bank $18. This confirms WRAM-to-VRAM transfer behavior but does not connect ROM banks $18-$1F to the uploaded data.

scenario_bytecode.dispatch_table: CPU $83:B2A7-$83:B338, ROM $01B2A7-$01B338; 73 words for command values $00-$48; entry $00 is $0000
scenario_bytecode.root_table: CPU $83:EA41-$83:EE96, ROM $01EA41-$01EE96; 370 three-byte selector slots, of which 356 are non-null pointers to 355 unique targets; slots $0161-$016E are null
scenario_bytecode.targets: slots $0000-$008F target CPU bank $91, $0090-$0121 target bank $92, and $0122-$0160 plus $016F-$0171 target bank $93; slots $0159-$015A duplicate target $93:BA88
scenario_bytecode.state: WRAM $0C39 is the 16-bit stream cursor, $0C3B is the stream bank, and $0C37 is the current command
scenario_bytecode.known_commands: $07 and $10 are zero-operand choice/menu commands at CPU $83:B9AA and $83:BFDE; $10 calls CPU $83:E600 to prepare the presentation, while $07 opens the prepared X/Y/B prompt through CPU $81:8000 and advances by only its opcode byte. $08 consumes a little-endian 16-bit selector and reaches the zero-terminated 16-bit text/glyph renderer at CPU $80:9A0E; $48 consumes one byte and branches on value $0A
scenario_bytecode.text_tables: Command $08 has 3,989 structurally bounded selector slots across $99:8000, $9A:8000, $9B:8000, $9C:8000, $9D:8000, $9E:8000, $9F:8000, and $98:C1C8. There are 3,558 non-null slots, 431 null slots, and 3,553 unique zero-terminated streams. The final plausible selector is $0F94; selector $0F95 reads $0120 and is outside the pointer-table model.
scenario_bytecode.text_streams: Across the bounded corpus, $0000 is the terminator, $000A is the only other word below $0100, and 716 distinct glyph codes occur. Unique stream targets do not overlap. Presentation data is separate at $98:8000 + (selector-$0200)*2: 3,394 non-null slots use ordinary portrait resource/variant pairs and resolve to 3,389 unique streams; 83 non-null slots use the $FF wide marker and distinct 21x8 streams; 81 low non-null selectors bypass the table and use default 16x8 dimensions. Among portrait-pair slots, 2,794 are multiline and 2,261 contain at least 16 glyph cells. The longest unique stream has 214 glyph cells, the maximum observed line width is 14 cells, and the largest structure has 36 line records.
scenario_bytecode.renderer_evidence: CPU $80:9A0E walks 16-bit words until $0000, treats $000A as a line break, and sends ordinary values to CPU $80:9B2C. CPU $80:9B2C maps $0100-$04FF to FastROM $B6:80A0, $0500-$08FF to $B7:8000, and $0900+ to $B6:BCA0. Each glyph is assembled from four 16-byte SNES 2bpp blocks at source +$000, +$010, +$100, and +$110 into a 16x16 bitmap; glyph origins advance by 12 pixels. A trusted clean boot reached scenario selector $0170, command $08 with text selector $07E1, renderer $80:9A0E, and glyph routine $80:9B2C at frame 436. The selected stream is $9C:9358 / ROM $0E1358, with 56 glyph words in four 14-cell lines, three $000A words, and a $0000 terminator.
scenario_bytecode.root_entry_text: All 355 unique root pointers begin with command values $01-$49. Exactly 100 roots begin directly with confirmed command $08 and reference 95 distinct valid, non-null text selectors. All 100 use ordinary portrait resource/variant presentation; 82 are multiline and 69 contain at least 16 glyph cells. This is confirmed root-entry coverage only and does not classify unmatched streams as unused.
scenario_bytecode.title_menu: Trusted October 10, 2026 input-driven traces confirmed that the opening menu family bypasses command $08. CPU $81:85DF-$81:8629 copies fixed title streams from $84:A1D8 / ROM $0221D8 (no save, 8/7 cells) or $84:A1FA / ROM $0221FA (valid save, 8/8/7 cells) to WRAM $0A00. The dispatch table at $81:831B routes New Game to a 9/8-cell stream at $84:A22E / ROM $02222E and Options to fixed sound-mode records at $84:A254/$84:A266 plus one of twenty $12-byte BGM records at $84:A278-$84:A3DF. All paths call $80:997B and send individual glyphs through $80:9B2C. Implemented English is New Game / Options, Continue / New Game / Options, Start New Game / Enter Password, Sound Stereo / Sound Mono, and BGM 00-19; explicit character offsets retain visual centering and native BGM numeral words are preserved.
scenario_bytecode.note: Direct reconstruction of the 40 distinct startup glyphs matches the completed screenshot, confirming the glyph layout and a local provisional mapping. Repository policy keeps the decoded passage and local character map out of tracked files. Runtime transfer evidence shows DMA channel 7 mode 1 uploads from WRAM $7E:8000/$7E:8800 to VRAM through $2118/$2119. Earlier trusted Mesen captures confirmed the centered title, both New Game choices, Sound Stereo / BGM 00, and incremented BGM 01 before the compositor redesign. A trusted October 6, 2026 trace confirmed that ordinary presentation pair $21,$01 selects the portrait visible with opening selector $07E5 and pair $00,$09 selects the portrait visible with $07E6; CPU $83:E2A8 uses the first byte to choose a graphics-resource descriptor through $83:EE97 and the second as its variant. Translated streams use bit 15 as a packed-Latin marker, with two independent 7-bit character IDs per existing word; the shared compositor renders each character at six-pixel spacing while bit-clear legacy words retain the original 12-pixel path. Generated localized name defaults use ordinary packed Latin, so insertion overwrites only the selected character and preserves the other nine positions. Legacy bit-15-clear name fields are blank-converted before their first packed insertion. The bounded name redraw restores the 8-tile compositor width before rendering both halves of each 16-pixel glyph. Trusted October 11, 2026 captures against translated ROM SHA-256 1091629245703d49d2b447ddde511559b84db12ba9847a44dfececb32890e73f confirmed Aiyah -> Biyah as a single-position overwrite and page-two Aiyah -> Áiyah with restored 8x10 dimensions and nonblank upper/lower staged tile rows. The 23rd World Tournament opening now validates deterministic same-bank text relocation in bank $99, including source hashing, reviewed free space, pointer updates, overlap checks, and decode round trips. Complete portrait-catalog naming remains unresolved. An earlier cursor-delta trace sampled stale $0C37 and shifted command attribution by one iteration; root $0170 actually begins with command $08.

font_regions.location: FastROM $B6:80A0-based and $B6:BCA0-based regions in ROM bank $36, plus FastROM $B7:8000-$B7:FFFF / ROM bank $37
font_regions.format: Each displayed character is a 16x16 bitmap assembled from four 16-byte SNES 2bpp blocks at source offsets +$000, +$010, +$100, and +$110. The renderer advances glyph origins by 12 pixels, allowing unused margins to overlap. Bank $37 has identical bitplane bytes in all 16,384 tile rows, so decoded pixels use indices 0 and 3; relevant bank-$36 data is not uniformly duplicated-plane and must not be generalized to the whole bank.
font_regions.evidence: The bounded text corpus uses 716 distinct codes: 185 in $0100-$02D0 from $B6:80A0, 403 in $0500-$08F7 from $B7:8000, and 128 in $0900-$0A30 from $B6:BCA0. Every used code has a complete non-wrapping four-block source. Reconstructing the startup stream's 40 distinct glyphs produces the same four-line image seen at runtime; $0272 is the only fully blank used lower-range glyph in the corpus and is structurally consistent with a space.
font_regions.note: The code-to-character map is only provisional and remains in ignored local working data. The renderer format and source addressing are confirmed; comprehensive character naming and English replacement glyph design remain future work.

emulator_automation.evidence: The pinned mesen-agent backend and snes-automate wrapper passed a redistributable synthetic LoROM test: SNES/S-CPU identification, a 24-bit execute breakpoint at CPU $00:800D, CPU-bus and physical WRAM reads, SNES ROM/WRAM/VRAM/OAM/CGRAM/register memory-space discovery, disassembly, instruction trace, complete state JSON, and a headless screenshot. A read-only project probe also loaded the pinned 2 MiB original ROM, exposed the expected $20000-byte WRAM and $10000-byte VRAM spaces, reported initial PC $00:8001, and captured one decoded frame. bsnes-plus remains available for interactive debugger and visual-viewer cross-checks.
emulator_automation.note: Clean boot now provides deterministic DBZ-specific Lua callbacks, renderer breakpoint hits, WRAM staging, screenshots, and DMA/VRAM-port correlation without controller input. Agreement with bsnes-plus and input-driven navigation beyond the startup narration remain to be validated.
